papers.title: $L^p$-isometries on idempotents
papers.abstract: We study surjective $L^p$-isometries on spaces of bounded idempotents in an infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. On each fixed positive finite-rank stratum, every surjective $L^p$-isometry, $1\leq p<\infty$, is implemented by a unitary or antiunitary operator, possibly composed with adjunction; no separability is required. The same conclusion holds for the operator norm, viewed as the $L^\infty$-norm. On a separable space, operator-norm isometries of the infinite-rank, infinite-corank sector admit the additional complement operation, as do surjective $L^p$-isometries between individual $L^p$-perturbation classes for $1\leq p<\infty$. For the extended $L^p$-metric on all idempotents, implementations may be chosen independently on finite-distance classes, subject to an explicit compatibility condition for matching infinite-rank classes. The proofs use similarity coordinates and metric blow-ups, followed by tangent-space splittings, nearest projections at the $L^1$ endpoint, or sharp Fredholm-index distance estimates. We also establish uniqueness of standard implementations and use essential-spectral invariants to obtain continuum many perturbation-class isometry types.

papers.title: Boundaries of groups with compact-by-amenable decomposition
papers.abstract: We look at the Liouville property (triviality of harmonic functions) of topological groups G relative to a compact subgroup K. We show that Gelfand pairs have this property. Furthermore, we show that this property holds if and only if G admits a product decomposition G = K S for an amenable subgroup S. We identify the Poisson and Furstenberg boundaries of these groups. This applies in particular to reductive algebraic groups over local fields.

papers.title: A Poisson boundary solution to Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and Kadison's problem on MASA
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every inclusion $M\subset P$ of countably decomposable von Neumann algebras with a normal faithful conditional expectation, $M\subset c(P)$ has the weak Dixmier property, where $c(P)$ is the continuous core of $P$. By Haagerup's characterization, we have a completely new proof of Connes' bicentralizer conjecture, independent of the recent proof of Houdayer--Marrakchi. By Marrakchi's characterization, we also prove his relative bicentralizer conjecture. We also give a new solution to Kadison's problem after Popa and Marrakchi: further assuming that $M$ and $P$ have separable preduals and $M'\cap P=\mathcal Z(M)$, then there is a maximal abelian subalgebra of $M$ that is also maximal abelian in $P$. The proofs are based on a Poisson boundary theory for general von Neumann algebras, developed here as an extension of the theory of Das--Peterson for finite von Neumann algebras. Once this theory is established, the proofs for Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and Kadison's problem are short (around 7 pages each) and self-contained, relying only on results established by 1990. In both proofs, no separate treatment is needed for the type $\mathrm{III}_1$ case.

papers.title: Martingale Transforms and Subsequence Estimates in Noncommutative \(L_p\)-Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a transference principle from martingale transform inequalities to subsequence estimates for weakly null sequences. As applications, for every von Neumann algebra $\M$, (1) we show that, every bounded sequence in the Haagerup space $L_1(\M)=\M_*$ has either a norm-convergent subsequence or a $2$-co-lacunary subsequence, answering an open problem of Parcet and Randrianantoanina; (2) we prove that every UMD Banach space has the uniform USP, which in particular yields uniform USP for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<\infty$, answering a question posed by Oikhberg and Spinu; (3) we answer an open problem of Haagerup, Rosenthal and Sukochev for the upper $\ell_p$ estimates for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<2$, in the affirmative; (4) we also answer the problem of whether every $2$-strictly singular operator on a noncommutative $L_1$-space is automatically Dunford--Pettis.

papers.title: Formalizing local gauge freedom via bi-equivariant groupoid algebras
papers.abstract: Gauge degrees of freedom appear in many different contexts. Here, we describe their emergence in the context of architected metamaterials built from self-coupling blocks with internal symmetries. Quantifying the dynamics requires choices of local frames and the many available options constitute the local gauge degrees of freedom of the problem. In the absence of internal symmetries, the dynamical matrices generating the dynamics are all built from the left regular representation of a groupoid C*-algebra canonically associated to the architecture. If the resonators display internal symmetries, we show that the mentioned groupoid C*-algebra accepts a natural 2-action by the group of internal symmetries and that the local gauge freedom can be encoded in a bi-equivariant sub-groupoid algebra generated from the mentioned 2-action. The latter is shown to be the smallest C*-algebra containing all dynamical matrices that can be engineered in a laboratory, for a given architecture and discrete group of internal symmetries.

papers.title: Unbounded traces, Connes' index theorem for measured foliations, and the Godbillon-Vey invariant in KK-theory
papers.abstract: We prove that unbounded positive traces define KK-elements with real coefficients. Such traces naturally arise from invariant transverse measures on foliations (Connes, 1979) and, more generally, on Lie groupoids (Crainic--Mestre, 2019). As an application, we build a canonical KK-element with real coefficients whose associated map of K-groups is the Godbillon-Vey invariant as constructed by Connes. In the process, we show how Connes' index theorem for measured foliations can be deduced from the Connes-Skandalis longitudinal index theorem, using cyclic cohomology.

papers.title: PHP decompositions and primitivity of group rings
papers.abstract: We show that every countable group $G$ that has Ozawa's property $\rm PHP$ and contains a non-abelian free subgroup has the following property: the group ring $KG$ is primitive for any field $K$. As a consequence, we greatly extend the previously existing results on the primitivity of group rings. New examples include linear groups and groups of homeomorphisms of the Cantor set. Along the way, we prove that the class of groups with $\rm PHP$ enjoys some permanence properties that are of independent interest.

papers.title: On the Principle of Localization on Quasi-Orbits in Crossed Products
papers.abstract: Quasi-regular $C^*$-dynamical systems with locally closed quasi-orbits are considered. For the corresponding crossed products, a localization principle on quasi-orbits is proven. This principle reduces the study of the primitive spectrum of the original crossed product to the study of the primitive spectra of crossed products, each corresponding to its own $C^*$-dynamical system with a single quasi-orbit. Assuming that the group action on the primitive spectrum of the $C^*$-algebra in the crossed product is free, except for some fixed subset, a characterization of the spectrum of the crossed product is provided, which allows for a description of the Jacobson topology on it.

papers.title: Fujita exponents on quantum Euclidean spaces
papers.abstract: We study the well-posedness of a non-linear heat equation with power nonlinearity with positive initial data on quantum Euclidean spaces. We prove a noncommutative analogue of the classical Fujita theorem by identifying the critical exponent separating finite-time blow-up from global existence for small initial data. Moreover, we establish a fundamental inequality in general semifinite von Neumann algebras that is of independent interest and plays a crucial role in the study of global existence and local well-posedness of solutions of nonlinear equations in noncommutative setting.

papers.title: Ascent and descent of operators concerning Jordan products
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal B(\mathcal X)$ be the algebra of all bounded linear operators on a Banach space $\mathcal{X}$ over the real or complex field $\mathbb F$ with $\dim\mathcal X \ge 3$. In this paper, we give several properties of the ascent (descent) of operators or Jordan products of operators in $\mathcal B(\mathcal X)$ and use these properties to characterize certain operators such as algebraic operators, rank-one, rank-two operators, rank-one nilpotent operators as well as some relations between operators in terms of ascent (descent) of Jordan products. As an application, we give a characterization, up to a multiplier of nonlinear functional $f:\mathcal B(\mathcal X)\to \mathbb F^*$, of ring isomorphisms of $\mathcal B(\mathcal X)$ in the case $\dim \mathcal X=\infty$ and Jordan isomorphisms of $\mathcal B(\mathcal X)$ in the case $\dim \mathcal X<\infty$ via the maps with range containing all operators of rank at most three that preserve the ascent of Jordan products of operators. A slightly different characterization in term of descent is also obtained.

papers.title: A Counterexample to Voiculescu's Normal Dilation Conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct a compact operator $T$ with trace class self-commutator and vanishing Helton-Howe measure such that $T\oplus S-M\notin \mathcal{S}_2$ for every bounded operator $S$ and every bounded normal operator $M$. This gives counterexamples to Voiculescu's normal dilation and stable classification conjectures. The construction uses magnetic shifts on finite square tori. Their real parts have commutators of uniformly bounded trace norm, while their frame errors admit logarithmic lower bounds in the lattice size. A summability criterion for frame error turns these finite-dimensional estimates into a compact counterexample. The same operator inequalities yield a rank profile invariant under Hilbert-Schmidt perturbations and normal stabilization, which distinguishes the example from zero.

papers.title: Abelian approximations for bicrossed products
papers.abstract: We propose a general framework to interpret the cocycle bicrossed product of a matched pair $G \bowtie H = D$ of locally compact quantum group as a deformation quantization of an extension $V \to \mathcal{G} \to G$ with $V$ abelian. This construction requires the existence of a $G$-equivariant measure class isomorphism $\eta_H : H \to \hat V$, which we call an abelian approximation of $H$. In the smooth case, the extension $\mathcal{G}$ naturally becomes equipped with a Lie-Poisson structure. When both $G$ and $H$ admit abelian approximations, the duality of the bicrossed products provides a unitary operator $\mathcal{F} : \mathrm{L}^2(\mathcal{G}) \to \mathrm{L}^2(\mathcal{G}^*)$, the Poisson-Fourier transform, which implements the quantum duality principle of Drinfel'd. We discuss the construction of abelian approximations from Lie bialgebras and present several classes of examples.
